description: We are a team of motivated university students passionate about technology, space exploration and creative problem-solving. Our skills include web development, programming, UI/UX design and presentation. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to combine our strengths to build an accessible, engaging and practical solution using NASA data. We are excited to meet you all, exchange ideas, make new friends and create wonderful memories throughout the hackathon!
summary:
AstraPulse is an offline-first health monitoring web app for astronauts on long-term missions, built by Team Algo-Rhythm for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Microgravity, isolation and heavy workloads can slowly change crew health, and communication delays mean astronauts often can’t get real-time help from Earth. AstraPulse helps crews notice and understand these changes themselves. The technology has five steps to help them: monitor the readings, detect changes against each astronaut’s personal baseline instead of one shared average, understand what caused the change, act by suggesting a safe next step, and follow up by keeping a local record.

It covers three areas. Body tracks vitals, exercise, radiation dose and a skin-image triage tool. Habitat monitors the cabin, including CO₂ against NASA’s ECLSS reference. Mind offers a daily check-in companion, Nova, and “Orbital Reset,” a short guided breathing break. Core views work without a connection, and the interface is available in English, Spanish and French. Design choices draw on NASA Open Data, ECLSS and Human Research Program sources.

This is significant as astronauts will be isolated from the Earth and will have to manage their health independently.
details:
Algo-Rhythm Astronaut Health Monitor is an offline-first, web-based decision-support system designed to assist astronauts on long-duration space missions in identifying health deterioration at an early stage. Developed by a six-person multidisciplinary team for NASA's International Space Apps Challenge 2026, it addresses the challenge of crew self-monitoring under conditions of delayed communication with Earth.

The system's central component is cardiovascular monitoring. Astronauts record blood pressure, heart rate, symptoms, and measurement context, which are then compared against an individual, in-mission baseline and evaluated across seven- and thirty-day trends. Each assessment yields one of three states, Stable, Observe, or Action Required, accompanied by an explanation of the contributing indicators and a set of recommended follow-up actions.

Complementary modules extend coverage to other aspects of crew wellbeing, including AI-assisted dermatological image triage, exercise compliance tracking, immune-surveillance trends, and simulated habitat environment monitoring. A wellness component, comprising guided breathing exercises and a virtual companion, addresses the psychological demands of isolation and confinement.

The application is implemented as a Next.js and React progressive web app, with data stored locally to ensure functionality without connectivity. It relies on synthetic data rather than real patients or devices.

The prototype is intended solely for decision support and education. It is not a medical device, and its clinical rules require validation by qualified professionals.
